title: The Atlantic sugar plantation system
summary: Columbus brought sugarcane to Hispaniola in 1493, and by the early 1500s the Spanish were building sugar mills there. African slaves were first imported to the Americas on the same island. One study calls sugar fundamental to the origins of global capitalism. Plantations spread across the Caribbean: in the 19th century, over 600 enslaved Africans worked under brutal conditions at Annaberg on St John alone.

uncertainty.note: Sugarcane was introduced to Hispaniola by Columbus on his second voyage in 1493, with commercial mill production taking root in the early 1500s; Caribbean plantation slavery lasted until nineteenth-century colonial emancipations.

audience_note: Describes the brutal origins of the transatlantic plantation complex, chattel slavery, extreme physical exploitation, and the catastrophic collapse of Indigenous Caribbean populations.
